doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sideman years: J.J., Tyree Glenn, Sweets
title: Records for J.J. Johnson and the boat to Europe
summary: J.J. recorded 'J is for Jazz' at Columbia before the tour, and Elvin enjoyed sailing on the S.S. Stockholm.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh I’d say almost a year. It was a long time. And I left to go with J.J in the latter part of 1957 in the summers. We went to Sweden and we went to Denmark- we were in Scandinavia. We made a record recording—before we went we made these records at Colombia Studios 32nd street: “J is for Jazz” and another album. It was really fun a lot of nice tunes on there and J.J., with his beautiful arrangements, he was a genius
So JJ called you to do a recording before your European tour? And this is your first trip overseas correct? Was that something special for you?
We went over on a boat you know-­

We went over on the S.S Stockholm. That was great trip. I never saw so much food in my life. You know if you’re going to Europe, get on a boat! That is the way to go. You don’t have to worry about this other bullshit! (Laughs) It’s sad that they don’t have steam ships anymore cause it’s the best way to go, and economical too!
